notes: This contract pins Umbra's opt-in, non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 receive-order interaction-development slice to the exact C++ Send Interaction and Receive Interaction surfaces exported by the Requirements Lab. It verifies only official signatures, declared exception sets, adapter symbols, and real Catch2 selectors. The separately listed joined-federate HLAsetSwitches selector exercises a bounded standards-specific MOM control path before ordinary routing; its semantics are traced in support-switches-service-requirements-contract.json and do not expand this receive-order delivery claim. The ordinary slice accepts only the non-timestamped Send Interaction overload; it selects a recipient's closest active subscribed class, projects sent parameters available at that received class, suppresses the sender, rechecks subscription immediately before delivery, preserves tag/producer/FOM-selected mandatory transportation data, and dispatches through the recipient's immediate or evoked callback model. A passive ordinary subscription remains declaration state but does not arrange a Receive Interaction callback. It always supplies a null sent-region pointer. Timestamped delivery, retraction, regions/DDM, directed interaction, FOM sharing-policy enforcement, custom transportation, save/restore, object delivery, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
